news.title: Binance Reports 98% Asset Replenishment After $6.34 Billion Theft
news.body: Binance said its October 29 theft followed a campaign beginning in June involving a compromised AI coding-tool installer, a fake recruitment assignment and stolen deployment credentials. In its November 3 report, the exchange said it had replenished 98% of affected token assets and frozen or intercepted approximately $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion affected. These company-reported figures do not represent independently audited recoveries: replenishment includes replacement assets funded by Binance, while freezing or interception does not establish their return to customers. Binance restored withdrawals in phases.

news.title: FIS Cuts Banking Growth Forecast as Client Conversions Slip
news.body: Delayed conversions involving fewer than 10 clients prompted FIS to reduce its 2026 pro forma Banking Solutions revenue-growth forecast to 3.5–4%, from 5–5.5%. FIS also lowered companywide growth guidance to 3.1–3.6%, from 4.5–5%. Management said some implementations now extend into the third quarter of 2027, although almost all delayed conversions remain contractually required. The delays push revenue into later delivery windows despite those commitments. Payments revenue grew 3%, with debit and credit issuer volumes consistent with preceding quarters.

news.title: OCC Sets Bank AI Examination Framework Without New Supervisory Expectations
news.body: The OCC issued a framework for examiners reviewing banks’ use of AI and agentic AI in ordinary business activities. Rather than establish a separate AI risk category, the framework supplements existing model-risk, governance, technology, compliance and operational-risk practices. It creates no new supervisory expectations and does not require banks to adopt a separate AI risk appetite. For payment-initiation and fraud-decision tools, examinations remain within existing safety-and-soundness practices; the framework does not grant approval to particular vendors.

news.title: Bilt Agrees to Buy Sports Loyalty Company Lava for $300 Million
news.body: Bilt agreed to acquire Lava for $300 million, connecting its residential and merchant rewards network with sports loyalty technology. Lava has relationships with 56 professional sports franchises and more than 300 technology adapters spanning POS, identity, ticketing, loyalty and payments. Bilt reports approximately seven million members across residential communities and partnerships with about 50,000 merchants. The proposed combination would link venue integrations with Bilt’s existing network, but the announcement does not quantify incremental payment volume, customer overlap or acquisition synergies.

news.title: Yellow Card Adds Brazilian Pix Capabilities Through GoMoney Acquisition
news.body: Yellow Card completed its acquisition of Brazilian virtual asset provider GoMoney in October, adding real-denominated collections and disbursements, including Pix, alongside stablecoin settlement. GoMoney has applied for central-bank authorization and continues operating under Brazil’s transitional regime; it has not completed full authorization. The company remains a wholly owned subsidiary led by its founders. Yellow Card gains domestic payment capabilities for Brazil-linked cross-border flows, although the announcement disclosed neither a transaction-cost advantage nor an increase in processing volume.
